images.name: 01_map_of_the_arena
images.final_prompt:
Create one landscape 16:9 illustrated map, 01_map_of_the_arena. Reference 1 style_map is ONLY the drawing style: top-down hand-drawn children's-book map on stained cream paper, coloured crayon scribbles, dark ink outlines, white rounded labels. Do not copy its attractions or rectangular layout. Reference 2 ref_plan supplies the round layout, north up. References 3 owner_ref and 4 tall_walls supply soft-play structure/material detail, translated into the illustration style.
A thick dark perfectly ROUND hall wall nearly fills the image height, fully visible with room for the entrance at bottom. The hall is 155 metres across. Inside, ONE dense continuous flat-topped twelve-storey block of soft-play extends right to the wall: yellow red blue green padded posts, black netting, coloured mat decks and tubes seen from above. No bare floor outside the small central court and corridors, no other attractions. NOT rings of steps or terraces. Two thin ring corridors run within the frame joined by short spoke corridors with a few little staircase symbols at junctions, per plan. These are level circulation paths through a dense structural grid, not concentric stepped seating. Only two narrow ring-shaped ledges close around the centre.
Exact centre: small round 25m court with blue-green checker floor, yellow clock-dial ring, short red padded post, and a child's crayon stick figure with "1 2 3" beside it. White rounded label "THE POST". Below the post a little green arrow points down, label "EXIT". A few solid-colour tube slides descend into court, one orange, one blue, one green.
Bottom/south: small low tunnel protrudes through the wall, red arrow pointing inward labelled "YOU ARRIVE HERE". Where tunnel meets wall a small blue gateway sign reads "PLAY ZONE". One straight pale-green path goes from gate north through frame to court. One big white rounded label across upper frame reads "THE BIG FRAME".
Exactly five labels, each once and correctly spelled: "THE BIG FRAME", "THE POST", "EXIT", "PLAY ZONE", "YOU ARRIVE HERE". Only other writing is child's "1 2 3". No title, compass lettering, legend, extra text, watermark, people (except drawn stick figure), arcade, ball pit, inflatables, restaurants, party rooms, or other attractions. Keep all labels and whole circular wall inside composition.
Precision for this attempt: the court diameter must be only one sixth the hall diameter, matching ref_plan. Pack dozens of tiny netted frame bays across the remaining footprint, so it reads as a huge continuous block. Ring circulation corridors must be thin lines within it. The clock ring has sixty little tick marks. All tube slides are entirely one colour, including joints: no contrasting yellow stripes on blue slides. Leave a slim paper margin above the complete circular wall.
images.weakness: Court remains oversized relative to 25m/155m; twelve-storey depth and the two narrow central ledges are not clearly conveyed, and clock ticks are irregular.

images.name: 04_the_whole_arena_from_above
images.final_prompt:
Create one photoreal landscape 16:9 concept image: 04_the_whole_arena_from_above. Reference 1 owner_ref sets exact materials, realism and abandoned lighting. Reference 2 tall_walls sets the sheer twelve-storey gallery walls (do not include its doll). Reference 3 ref_plan sets round footprint and south entrance. Reference 4 ref_section sets the vertical section: twelve stacked floors, only two narrow 4m ledges at floors four/eight, and otherwise sheer walls. Do not reproduce diagram text.
High three-quarter aerial view of the WHOLE round hall with roof cut away, from above the south side looking north. Fit complete circular concrete perimeter and entrance in frame. Hall diameter 155 metres, height 42 metres. ONE solid huge block of soft-play frame fills the wall-to-wall footprint, twelve storeys / 34 metres high everywhere. Top is a huge flat dense roofscape of netted coloured mat decks, crawl tubes, slide tops and padded post grid like roofs of a city, all at the same height. Frame extends solidly from centre shaft all the way to concrete wall. No empty annulus or bare hall floor.
In exact centre a small round vertical shaft opens like a deep well or interior of a silo/colosseum. Court at its bottom is only 25 metres across (one sixth hall diameter). Shaft sides are curved sheer walls of real walkable galleries stacked twelve storeys deep: four storeys vertically, one narrow ledge, four more vertically, another narrow ledge, four more vertically, no wide terraces. Twelve floors clearly discernible with black knotted safety netting, yellow/red/blue/green vinyl-padded steel posts, coloured vinyl mat decks, square red bubble-window panels, crawl tubes and punch bags. Solid-colour glossy orange, blue and green tube slides hang down the gallery face. Each slide is entirely ONE colour, no contrasting stripes.
Small bright court deep below has worn blue-and-green checker foam puzzle-mat floor, yellow painted clock ring and short red padded post at exact centre. Exactly two thin net bridges span shaft above court. In foreground, straight narrow entrance lane cuts a deep canyon through twelve-storey block from small low padded gateway in south wall to court, blue-green checker floor between net fences. Clearly show tall vertical canyon walls. No text on gateway or anywhere.
Photoreal materials and dusty abandoned quiet atmosphere exactly like owner_ref. Sparse cold white fluorescent lighting, dim pools of light, long shadows, haze. Roof removed for aerial visibility, small perimeter steel truss remnants only if needed. Whole hall readable, deep central court visible. No people, children, doll/entity, animals, arcade machines, neon, inflatables, ball pit, separate attractions, striped slides, labels, lettering, HUD, UI, watermark. Crucial geometry: FLAT-TOPPED DENSE BLOCK with SMALL STEEP SHAFT, never a bowl of broad concentric steps.
GEOMETRY PRECISION: The circular concrete wall directly touches the outermost padded posts, with ZERO walkway, service corridor or exposed floor between wall and frame. There is only ONE circular concrete wall, not a circular raised platform inside a larger warehouse. View from outside and above that single hall wall with roof removed. All twelve floors must be countable on the far interior shaft face as twelve tightly stacked gallery rows, four rows between each narrow ledge. Entrance canyon is twelve storeys deep. Two narrow ledges are visible inside shaft. Avoid turning the front block into just three storeys or setting frame on a concrete pedestal. Keep the same flat top across entire frame.
images.weakness: Twelve storeys and two narrow ledges remain visually ambiguous; the rear hall wall is cropped and the roofscape has some uneven heights.
